newsitem.title: FINLAND: Aamulehti plans new Finnish media major.
newsitem.headline: Aamulehti plans new Finnish media major.

text.p: Finnish media group Aamulehti Oy said on Tuesday it planned to merge with domestic commercial broadcaster MTV Oy, creating a new major in the Finnish communication business.

In a statement detailing its plans, Aamulehti said the new company, with net annual sales around 2.5 billion markka and 2,600 full-time employees, would also be strong also amid accelerating international competition.
Aamulehti plans new Finnish media major
Aamulehti said the new company to be formed would have a strong market share in the print, electronic and audiovisual sectors and be a front-runner in the area of new media and digital technology.
"This newly signed agreement is an answer to many open questions about the future of the Finnish communication business," Aamulehti CEO Matti Packalen said in the statement.
Both companies have had strong earnings in recent years and the merger would guarantee strength in the balance sheet and profitability of the new company from the start, it said.
"Combining these two strong companies ... will bring an important media consolidation also at the European level," Packalen said.
Pending approval by the authorities for the deal, Aamulehti shares would be converted into the new company's shares at one-to-one with shares in MTV converted at one to 137.5.
The new company would be entered in the trade register at the start of 1998 and seek a bourse listing, Aamulehti said.
The companies' main shareholders now are wholesaler Kesko Oy, Swedish media group Marieberg Tidnings Ab, bank Merita Oy, telecoms group Nokia Oy and insurer Pohjola.
